label: copy-phase input token o
explanation: Fires when the token o is fed back as input during the copy phase (i.e. the model just emitted o and is now recalling the following original token). 99.6% of activation mass is on in_tok == o in copy phase; essentially silent in the original phase (56 weak activations) and at the delimiter, and does not fire on o in the original prefix. Magnitude is largest when o was the first original token (o is the first copy input, recall_idx 1, ~3.2 = max) and decays with how late in the copy the o appears; a repeated o after an earlier o in the copy is weaker (e.g. 0.33 vs 0.97). False positives are o inputs late in the copy phase (recall_idx >= 5), especially after an earlier o, where it often stays off. Tiny residual weak activations (<0.1 of max) on copy-phase b/u at recall_idx 1.

issues: Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.857, R 0.957, F1 0.904, mass recall 0.996.

Phase claims hold. The original phase has 56 weak activations (5e-5 of the mass) and the delimiter has 0. in_tok o holds 99.6% of the mass and has 31x lift. Leftovers are b, u, v and h at a few tenths of a percent of the mass.
Magnitude claim holds. The top activations (about 1.0 of max) are all o at recall_idx 1, i.e. sequences that start with o. first_tok o takes 38% of the mass.

The false positives are systematic but already disclosed: precision drops with copy position. Precision is 1.0 at recall_idx 1-3, 0.97 at 4, 0.64 at 5, 0.44 at 6, 0.48 at 7 and 0.67 at 8. Split by to_go it falls from 0.91 at to_go 3 to 0.73 at to_go 0. This looks like activation strength decaying until it drops below threshold, not a separate class: n_digits, L, earlier o's and earlier b/u/v do not cleanly separate the late misses.
Tighter predicates do not beat the original on test F1: recall_idx<=4 gets 0.867, recall_idx<=5 gets 0.896, and (recall_idx<=4)|(n_digits==0) gets 0.892. So the simpler predicate is justified.
